mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 8.5% within one month signals severe labor market deterioration, triggering immediate equity sell-offs as consumer spending and corporate margins contract.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 8.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >50% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) by >0.5% in one month indicate broad demand contraction, causing S&P 500 returns to fall over 60 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline >0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS decline >0.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >40% of instances over 10-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL >3.0% YoY) triggers aggressive monetary tightening, reducing S&P 500 returns over 20 days as higher discount rates depress equity valuations.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL >3.0% periods, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of cases over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS >100k monthly) consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when PAYEMS increases >100k monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 95.0 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to reduced corporate output and investment.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95.0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: When INDPRO remains below 95.0 for two months, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >45% of cases over 10-year periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and residential construction (HOUST) by >0.3% in one month indicate systemic supply-side disruption, driving S&P 500 returns negative over 20 days through reduced economic activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both decline >0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: When INDPRO and HOUST decline >0.3%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >40% of instances over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle economic expansions with GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% annually drive positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days through strong consumer demand and corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >50% of cases when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annually.
